Historical August baselines for Warsaw (typical highs ~21–23°C) place this outcome on the warmer side of average but consistent with recent warm-air advection patterns.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Jinnah International Airport in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, showers, and high humidity are capping daytime heating in Toronto on August 31, keeping the highest temperature tightly clustered in the 22–24 °C range according to the latest model guidance.** Official Environment Canada forecasts call for showers with a thunderstorm risk and a daytime high of 24 °C under mostly cloudy skies, while several private models project 21–23 °C amid widespread overcast conditions and periods of light-to-moderate rain. 

These conditions suppress solar insolation compared with clearer late-summer days, limiting surface warming despite near-seasonal averages (historical mean high ~24.5 °C). Light southeasterly flow advects moist air, sustaining high dew points and preventing strong diurnal temperature rises, while any embedded convection could briefly enhance or suppress local maxima depending on timing. 

Market-implied odds reflect this narrow scientific uncertainty: Environment Canada’s 24 °C call edges out slightly higher probability, yet ensemble spread and private-model consensus around 22–23 °C keep those outcomes nearly as likely. Newer model runs or radar trends on the morning of the 31st could shift the precise high by 1–2 °C within this window.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model guidance from sources including WeatherBug, AccuWeather, and regional ensembles points to a daytime high near 23–24 °C in Mexico City on September 1, aligning with the market’s heaviest trading on those two outcomes. Early-September climatology features a transition from the warmer, drier late-summer regime toward the rainy season peak, when frequent afternoon convection and cloud cover typically cap temperatures 1–3 °C below August averages. Current forecasts show scattered thunderstorms and southeasterly flow that should limit full insolation, keeping the daily maximum from reaching 25 °C or higher while also preventing a sharper drop below 23 °C. With resolution only 48 hours away, traders are weighting the latest short-range model runs most heavily, producing the observed concentration around the 23–24 °C bracket.
